findings.title: submit_claim and record_settlement skip notice/evidence gates; late notices still mark notice_compliant; DRAFT→SETTLED forges award amounts
findings.description: ClaimsDocumentor documents Notice → Document → Quantify → Submit → Negotiate and maintains notice_compliant plus check_notice_deadlines(), but submit_claim() only sets ClaimStatus.SUBMITTED with no check of notice_compliant, overdue notices, evidence, narrative, or damage support. record_notice_sent() sets notice_compliant = all(n.sent) without comparing sent_date to event_date+deadline_days, so overdue contractual notices still flip notice_compliant True. record_settlement() writes SETTLED, time_awarded_days, and amount_awarded from any prior status including DRAFT with no UNDER_REVIEW/approval gate. calculate_delay_damages()/add_damage_calculation() accept unbounded daily_rate/amount that feed cost_claimed. Distinct from already-reported schedule-delay EOT forge and warranty update_claim_status APPROVED.
findings.impact: A contractor/agent can mint a multi-million SETTLED claim award (PoC: $4.635M delay package submitted with notice_compliant=False; $1M DRAFT→SETTLED; late differing-conditions notices still notice_compliant=True) used as the live claims register for recovery/payment negotiation—claim inflation and preservation of contractually forfeited notice rights.
attack_path: 1. Operator deploys ClaimsDocumentor from this skill as the project claims system of record.
2. Attacker create_claim(DELAY) then calculate_delay_damages(delay_days=90, daily_rate=50000) with no notices sent (notice_compliant remains False).
3. Attacker submit_claim(claim_id) → SUBMITTED despite overdue/unsent Intent to Claim and Detailed Claim notices.
4. Optionally record_settlement(claim_id, 90, cost_claimed) or, on a fresh DRAFT claim, record_settlement directly with amount_awarded=1000000 → SETTLED.
5. Alternate path: after deadlines expire, record_notice_sent for each type → notice_compliant True; submit_claim proceeds as if timely.
findings.remediation: Block submit_claim unless notice_compliant and every notice sent_date <= deadline; require authenticated evidence and non-empty narrative/damages. Allow record_settlement only from UNDER_REVIEW/NEGOTIATING with dual-control approver. Cap damage inputs; surface overdue notices as hard failures, not advisory rows.

findings.title: review_submission(approved=True) stamps APPROVED from NOT_STARTED with empty file_path and no submission record
findings.description: AsBuiltTracker.review_submission() is the production approval path for handover drawings. It never requires DocumentStatus.SUBMITTED, a prior DocumentSubmission, non-empty file_path, or revision evidence. Calling review_submission(doc_id, approved=True, ...) on a NOT_STARTED document with file_path="" sets status=APPROVED and approved_date. get_summary() then reports completion_rate=100 and approved counts used for handover readiness. Distinct from already-reported Innovative as-built-documentation empty-FINAL completeness forge (different skill/API).
findings.impact: Handover/closeout can show 100% as-built approval with zero drawings on file. Occupancy, final payment, and O&M turnover proceed on a false documentation-complete signal; missing as-builts create safety/operations liability.
attack_path: 1. Operator deploys AsBuiltTracker as the as-built register (Quick Start / get_summary / export_to_excel).
2. Documents are seeded via add_document (status NOT_STARTED, file_path empty).
3. Attacker (colluding PM/contractor) calls review_submission(document_id, approved=True, reviewer='PM') without record_submission.
4. Document becomes APPROVED; get_summary().completion_rate reaches 100% with submitted_date still None and no file.
5. Export/transmittal/handover package treats the register as complete.
findings.remediation: Allow review_submission only when status is SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW and the latest submission has a non-empty file_path. Reject approve when no DocumentSubmission exists. Keep completion_rate based on verified files, not reviewer string alone.
